author: blu
body: The anchor is the name of the definition the block describes: the template's own name where the template carries one (the author's explicit claim), otherwise the nearest def or type-def that follows the block in the source. An empty anchor means no definition follows. The offset is the source offset of the prose line, recorded at collection so the anchoring pass can order blocks against defs.

author: blu
body: prose-blocks and annotations carry the per-definition record through to emission: each prose block holds the anchor naming the definition the block describes, and each annotation already names its target. Both lists are empty unless the compile ran with the prose flag or the source carried annotations; the text emitters print them so a downstream reader can pair prose with the definition it belongs to.
